novel_features.name: New-since award watch
novel_features.description: See which award seats appeared on a route since you last looked, from your synced local data.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a first-seen timestamp on every locally synced availability row, which no live API call or wrapper provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user asks what changed or what is new on a route, instead of re-running a full search and diffing by eye.

novel_features.name: Credit-aware recheck
novel_features.description: Re-verify aging award rows are still live right before booking. It performs one live quota probe per run (1 daily call), and --apply is refused when quota is unknown unless --ignore-quota is passed.
novel_features.rationale: Joins local synced_at ages with the credit-metered refresh endpoint and its quota block, guarding the 1,000-call daily budget no wrapper tracks.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Print-only by default: lists the aging rows it would refresh, their age, and the remaining daily quota (one probe call). Add --apply to spend refresh credits; --apply is refused when the quota is unknown unless --ignore-quota is passed.

novel_features.name: Cross-program direct-only scan
novel_features.description: Find direct-flight award seats under a mileage ceiling across every synced program at once.
novel_features.rationale: The bulk availability endpoint serves one program per call; the cross-program direct-only join exists only in the local store.
novel_features.example: seats-aero-pp-cli direct-scan --origin JFK --destination NRT --cabin business --max-mileage 90000 --sources united,virginatlantic,aeroplan --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this over the awards search when the user wants nonstop-only results across programs from already-synced data with zero API calls.

novel_features.name: Cabin/date calendar matrix
novel_features.description: Turn one route's synced availability into a date-by-cabin matrix you can scan at a glance.
novel_features.rationale: Pivots the flat bulk feed into the calendar shape shortlist-building actually needs, entirely from local rows.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when the user asks which dates have business or first availability on a route; it answers from the local store in one shot.

novel_features.name: Nonstop reach finder
novel_features.description: Discover where your miles can take you nonstop from one airport, ranked by cost and cross-checked against real dated seats.
novel_features.rationale: Chains the destinations fan-out with locally synced availability so the cheapest theoretical fares are confirmed against bookable dates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user has miles but no fixed destination. It has no local mode, and results is an object {origin, cabin, max_mileage, source, destinations[]} rather than a bare array. --confirm-live makes up to 10 extra live /search calls (opt-in; never under the test harness).

narrative.headline: Every Seats.aero Partner API endpoint, plus a local award-availability store that tells you what is new, what is still live, and where your miles reach nonstop.
narrative.value_prop: seats-aero-pp-cli wraps all seven Partner API endpoints (cached search, bulk availability, trips, routes, destinations, refresh, live) with agent-native output, then syncs routes and availability into typed SQLite tables. That local store powers new-since, calendar, direct-scan, reach and a quota-guarded recheck, none of which a thin wrapper or the web app can do.
narrative.auth_narrative: Seats.aero Pro subscribers create a Partner API key under Settings, then export it as SEATS_AERO_API_KEY. Keys are Pro-tier (1,000 calls per day, resets at midnight UTC; the X-RateLimit-Remaining header tracks it) or commercial-agreement keys. Pro keys cannot call live search and commercial keys cannot call refresh; doctor reports the remaining daily calls and which tier your key appears to be.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the key is picked up and see the remaining daily quota
Cheapest business-class awards JFK to LHR across every program in one call
Pull the tracked route atlas into the local store
Bulk calendar for one program, ready to pipe into jq
Where 90k miles get you nonstop from JFK, confirmed against dated seats

troubleshoots.fix: Live search needs a commercial-agreement key; Pro keys are rejected by design. Use awards (cached search) instead.

troubleshoots.symptom: HTTP 429 or requests rejected until tomorrow
troubleshoots.fix: The Pro daily quota of 1,000 calls is exhausted; run seats-aero-pp-cli doctor --json to see x-ratelimit-remaining and reset seconds, and prefer local commands (calendar, direct-scan, new-since) until it resets.

sync and sync --resources availability cannot populate availability because the endpoint requires source. Run seats-aero-pp-cli sync --resources availability --resource-param availability:source=<program> --since 7d once per program; routes needs no parameter. Then re-run; local commands never call the API.

Refresh credits are separate from daily calls and reset on the schedule in the response quota block. recheck is print-only by default but performs one live quota probe per run (1 daily call); --apply is refused when quota is unknown unless --ignore-quota is passed.

narrative.when_to_use: Use seats-aero-pp-cli whenever an agent needs award-flight availability by mileage program: cheapest awards on a route, a program's calendar, nonstop reach from an airport, or verifying a cached seat before booking. It is the right tool for miles-and-points redemption research and for building a local award-availability corpus that can be queried offline.
anti_triggers: Do not use it to book or ticket a flight; it reports availability only and never books.
Do not use it for cash fares, hotel awards, points valuations, or transfer-partner math; the Partner API carries none of that.
Do not use it to set push alerts; Seats.aero alerts are a web-app feature, use new-since on a schedule instead.
Do not expect live search with a Pro key; that endpoint is commercial-agreement only.

recipes.title: Cheapest business awards across all programs, narrowed for an agent
recipes.command: seats-aero-pp-cli awards --origin-airport SFO --destination-airport NRT --cabins business --order-by lowest_mileage --take 10 --agent --select data.Date,data.Route.Source,data.JMileageCost,data.JDirect
recipes.explanation: One cached search across every program, with --select trimming the wide availability rows to the four fields that matter.

recipes.title: What appeared since yesterday
recipes.explanation: Diffs the local availability table on first_seen_at, so only genuinely new rows come back.

recipes.title: Verify before you book, without spending credits
recipes.explanation: Print-only by default: lists the aging rows it would refresh, their age, and the remaining daily quota (one probe call). Add --apply to spend refresh credits.

recipes.title: Direct-only under 90k miles across three programs
recipes.command: seats-aero-pp-cli direct-scan --origin JFK --destination NRT --cabin business --max-mileage 90000 --sources united,virginatlantic,aeroplan --agent
recipes.explanation: A cross-program join over synced data that the one-program-per-call bulk endpoint cannot answer.

recipes.title: Where can 90k miles take me nonstop
